mainTopic: Reading unclear money amounts in a שטר: the holder gets the lower amount, and 'דינרי' (gold) differs from 'דינרין' (silver) (בבא בתרא קסו.)
overview: The גמרא is working through a ברייתא about a שטר that names a metal (gold or silver) and 'dinars' without saying exactly how much. First it asks whether a gold amount could mean tiny coins, and answers that people don't make tiny gold coins. Then it asks why 'זהב בדינרין' isn't read as the bigger amount. אביי answers that when a שטר is unclear, the holder gets the lower amount. That causes a problem in the רישא, where the ברייתא gives the bigger amount. רב אשי solves it: the רישא is where the שטר wrote 'דינרי', meaning gold dinars, and the סיפא is where it wrote 'דינרין', meaning silver dinars. The גמרא proves this from a story: bird pairs in ירושלים cost gold דינרי, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל swore to bring the price down to plain דינרין, meaning cheap silver coins.

steps.title: Maybe the document means small coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier ruling: why not say the שטר means small change (פריטי) rather than a full dinar?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say it means small coins?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ruling just discussed and suggests a smaller reading of the שטר: maybe it means small coins, not a full dinar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wording is unclear, maybe the lender only gets a few small coins. That would be a smaller amount than what the ברייתא gave him. The גמרא wants to know why that reading is not used.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (opens a challenge with a different reading)

phrases.english: But say it means small coins!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of the ברייתא from before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading of the coin amount in the שטר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unclear שטר could mean a smaller amount, small coins, so why give a full dinar?

steps.title: Nobody makes small gold coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people do not mint small coins out of gold, so 'gold' can't mean small change.
steps.simpleTranslation: People do not make small coins out of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: small coins are never made of gold, so the שטר can't mean that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reading only works if it matches how people actually use money. Since small change is never made of gold, 'gold' in the שטר must mean a real gold coin.

keyTerms.meaning: People don't do (it); not normal practice

phrases.english: Small coins of gold, people do not make.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: the suggested reading doesn't match how coins are made.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שטר might mean small coins.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gold small coins don't exist, so the full gold coin reading stands.

steps.title: The ברייתא on 'gold in dinars'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause: if the שטר says 'gold in dinars', he gets gold worth at least two silver dinars.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Gold in dinars': no less than two silver dinars' worth of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא to set up its next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטר says 'gold' and 'dinars' (plural, so at least two). The ברייתא reads it as gold worth two silver dinars, which is the smaller of the possible values.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin; it can be silver or gold, and a gold dinar is worth much more

phrases.english: If it says: 'Gold in dinars'

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פָּחוֹת מִבִּשְׁנֵי דִינָרִין כֶּסֶף, זָהָב.
phrases.english: no less than two silver dinars' worth of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָהָב בְּדִינָרִין אֵין פָּחוֹת מִבִּשְׁנֵי דִינָרִין כֶּסֶף זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Gold in dinars' means gold worth two silver dinars.

steps.title: Why not two gold dinars' worth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the שטר isn't read as gold pieces worth two gold dinars.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means pieces of gold worth two gold dinars!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a different, bigger reading: maybe 'dinars' here means gold dinars, since the שטר is talking about gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא chose silver dinars as the measure. But the שטר mentions gold, so maybe the dinars are gold too, which would mean a much bigger amount. Both readings seem to fit the words.

phrases.english: But say: pieces of gold
worth two gold dinars is what he means!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא דַּהֲבָא פְּרִיכָא בִּתְרֵי דִינָרֵי דַּהֲבָא קָאָמַר
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice of silver dinars as the measure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the שטר speaks of gold, the dinars could be gold dinars, making the amount much larger.

steps.title: אביי: the holder of the שטר gets the lower amount
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that when a שטר is unclear, the holder of the שטר is at a disadvantage and gets the smaller amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The holder of the document has the lower hand.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי admits the bigger reading is possible, but gives a rule: in an unclear שטר, we go with the reading that is worse for the one holding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one holding the שטר wants to collect, so he has to prove his claim. Anything the שטר doesn't clearly say, he can't collect. So we use the cheaper reading, silver dinars.

keyTerms.meaning: The holder of the document has the lower hand; unclear wording goes against him
The one holding the document (the one trying to collect)

steps.whatToRemember: An unclear שטר is read against the one holding it: he collects only the smaller possible amount.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for reading all documents and contracts in הלכה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The hand of the document holder is on the bottom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי יַד בַּעַל הַשְּׁטָר עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule for reading documents decides between two possible readings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שטר might mean two gold dinars' worth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the wording is unclear, the holder gets the smaller amount: two silver dinars' worth.

steps.title: Then why does the רישא give the bigger amount?
steps.stepSummary: Using אביי's rule, the גמרא challenges the first clause: 'silver in dinars' gets two gold dinars' worth of silver, so why not the smaller amount?
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause teaches: 'Silver in dinars' means no less than two gold dinars' worth of silver. Why? Say it means pieces of silver worth two silver dinars!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns אביי's rule against the first part of the ברייתא, where the holder was given the larger amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא the ברייתא measured in gold dinars, the larger value. But by אביי's rule, an unclear שטר should get the smaller reading, two silver dinars. So the רישא seems to go against the rule.

phrases.english: The first clause, which teaches: 'Silver in dinars'

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנֵי דִּינָרִין זָהָב, כֶּסֶף;
phrases.english: no less than two gold dinars' worth of silver;
why? Say it means silver pieces
worth two silver dinars is what he means!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses אביי's rule from step 5 to attack the רישא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רישא of the ברייתא (silver in dinars gets two gold dinars' worth).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the holder always gets the lower reading, the רישא should give only two silver dinars' worth.

steps.title: רב אשי: different spellings mean different dinars
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the רישא is a case where the שטר wrote 'דינרי' and the סיפא is where it wrote 'דינרין', and each spelling means a different coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The first clause is where he wrote 'דינרי'; the last clause is where he wrote 'דינרין'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי solves the problem: the two clauses are not unclear at all, because the spelling of 'dinars' in the שטר shows which coin is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דינרי' refers to gold dinars, so in the רישא the amount is clear: two gold dinars' worth. 'דינרין' refers to silver dinars, so in the סיפא it is two silver dinars' worth. אביי's rule is only needed when the wording is truly unclear.
steps.whatToRemember: The spelling in the שטר decides the coin: 'דינרי' means gold dinars, 'דינרין' means silver dinars. Only when the wording is truly unclear does the holder get the lower amount.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא as quoted says 'בדינרין' in both clauses. רב אשי is telling us to read the רישא as if it said 'דינרי', so don't look for that word in the ברייתא's text.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The first clause is where he wrote 'dinarei',
phrases.notes: Read the רישא as if the שטר said 'דינרי', which the גמרא takes to mean gold dinars.

phrases.english: the last clause is where he wrote 'dinarin'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי רֵישָׁא דִּכְתַב דִּינָרֵי סֵיפָא דִּכְתַב דִּינָרִין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two clauses by different wording in the שטר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses use the same unclear wording, so the רישא goes against אביי's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא has the wording for gold dinars and the סיפא has the wording for silver dinars, so neither clause is unclear.

steps.title: Where do we see the two spellings mean different coins?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that דינרי and דינרין really mean different things.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know that there is a difference between "דינרי" and "דינרין"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants proof for רב אשי's answer from step 7. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's whole answer depends on the idea that one small spelling change gives a different coin. The גמרא does not want to rely on that without evidence. So it asks where we see that people actually used these two words differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (a request for a source)
Dinars, in the form used for gold coins
Dinars, in the plain form, meaning silver coins

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that there is a difference between "dinarei" and "dinarin"?
phrases.notes: These are the two spellings רב אשי used in step 7 to tell the רישא and the סיפא apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source to back up רב אשי's distinction in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that דינרי and דינרין mean different coins.

steps.title: The teaching about a woman who owes several bird offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching. A woman who might owe five offerings brings just one. A woman who definitely owes five brings one now and still owes the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: a woman who may have had five births, or may have had five זיבות, brings one קרבן and may then eat from קרבנות. She does not owe the rest. If she definitely had five births or five זיבות, she brings one קרבן and may then eat from קרבנות, but she still owes the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its proof by quoting a teaching about bird offerings. This part only sets up the background; the key words about coins come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman after birth or after a זיבה must bring a bird offering before she may eat קרבנות. If she is unsure about her cases, one offering is enough. If all five are certain, the original ruling makes her owe all five. That strict ruling made many people need birds, which is the background for the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Irregular bleedings that make a woman a זבה

phrases.english: As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיוּ עָלֶיהָ סְפֵק חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת;
phrases.english: A woman who has on her an uncertainty of five births;
or an uncertainty of five discharges –
brings one offering and may eat from sacrifices,
and the rest are not an obligation on her.
If she had five definite births;
or five definite discharges –
she brings one offering and may eat from sacrifices,
but the rest are an obligation on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 8's question by quoting the source that holds the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That דינרי and דינרין mean different coins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching about a woman's bird offerings. This step gives its background ruling.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל brings the bird price down from gold to silver
steps.stepSummary: Bird pairs cost gold דינרי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל swore to bring the price down to דינרין, and he did it by teaching that a woman owes only one offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It once happened that bird pairs in ירושלים cost gold dinars. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: "By this Holy House! I will not go to sleep tonight until they cost silver dinars." He went into the בית דין and taught: a woman who definitely had five births or five זיבות brings one קרבן and may then eat from קרבנות, and she does not owe the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual proof. The story uses דינרי for the expensive gold price and plain דינרין for the cheap price he wanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wanted to drop the price a great deal, so דינרין must mean something much cheaper than gold, which is silver. This shows that the plain spelling דינרין means silver coins and is different from דינרי, which was used here for gold. That supports רב אשי's reading of the רישא and סיפא in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of birds brought as offerings
I will sleep, or I will stay the night

steps.whatToRemember: Plain דינרין means silver coins, and דינרי can go with gold. That is the proof that the two spellings mean different coins, as רב אשי said in step 7.
steps.confusionAlert: The ruling that the woman owes only one offering is not the point for our sugya. The proof comes from the words in the story: gold דינרי versus plain דינרין, meaning silver.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proof supports רב אשי's answer, so the two clauses of the שטר ברייתא no longer conflict with אביי's rule.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וְעָמְדוּ קִינִּים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּדִינְרֵי זָהָב,
phrases.english: There was an incident where bird pairs in Jerusalem stood at gold dinars,
phrases.notes: "Stood at" means that was their price.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
By this Abode!
phrases.notes: He is swearing by the בית המקדש, the place of the שכינה.

phrases.english: I will not lie down tonight
until they are at dinarin.
phrases.notes: This is the key word for our proof. Here דינרין means the cheap silver coins.

phrases.english: He entered the court and taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיוּ עָלֶיהָ חָמֵשׁ לֵידוֹת וַדָּאוֹת;
phrases.english: A woman who had five definite births;
or five definite discharges –
brings one offering and may eat from sacrifices,
and the rest are not an obligation on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה וְעָמְדוּ קִינִּים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּדִינְרֵי זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source begun in step 9 and gives the actual wording that answers step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That דינרי and דינרין mean different coins, as רב אשי said.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's oath to bring the price down from gold דינרי to plain דינרין, which means silver.
